name: the-living-atlas
title: The Living Atlas
question: The thesis of the investigation — one typed interface, many mechanisms — is proven at the level of a single figure (Fig 6). Does it also hold at the level of a WHOLE CELL? This capstone assembles a composed whole cell in the figures' style — cell–environment uptake, a viability-gated Fig 6 metabolism, a viability monitor, and the division and disintegration rewrites, wired through shared cell and environment stores — and then SWAPS the Fig 6 metabolism behind identical ports (coarse, saturating kinetic, or real COBRApy FBA). Same cell, three mechanisms: does each produce its own life history while the interface never moves, and does each cell still grow, divide (mass-conserved), and die?
biological_summary: This is the payoff, and it is the paper's thesis carried up to the whole cell. The cell is ASSEMBLED BY HAND in the figures' style (meta_modelers_guide/wholecell.py) — it is NOT emitted by the compiler from the figure drafts. What it demonstrates is mechanism-swapping (Fig 6, law 4) at the WHOLE-CELL level: behind one unchanged metabolism interface (nutrients ⇒ biomass), the Fig 6 mechanism is selectable — ``build_whole_cell(metabolism="coarse"|"kinetic"|"fba")`` — and the same cell lives three DISTINCT life histories. With the COARSE lumped-yield metabolism the cell peaks at biomass 5.78 and divides at t≈3.0; with the SATURATING-KINETIC (Michaelis–Menten) metabolism it peaks at 6.43 and divides earlier, t≈2.1; with the REAL COBRApy FBA metabolism (flux-balance over e_coli_core solved each step) it peaks at 6.05 and divides at t≈2.7. Three mechanisms, three trajectories, one interface that does not move. In every case the cell first GROWS on the environmental nutrient as viability-gated metabolism converts uptake to biomass; once biomass crosses the division threshold the rewrite fires ONCE, partitioning the mother's biomass — division CONSERVES MASS (the mother is halved, not doubled) — so cell_count goes 1 → 2. Then a SCRIPTED thermal shock (the ThermalEnvironment process drives temperature 37 → 50 °C at a hard-coded t=12) pushes the cell out of its tolerance band; the viability monitor reads the interface and collapses viability 1.0 → 0.018, which gates metabolism off and triggers the disintegration rewrite — the maintained boundary fails and biomass decays into molecular debris (debris accumulating to ≈5.5–6.1, depending on the metabolism). Grow, divide once, die — but the "grow" and "divide" are mechanism-driven and mechanism-dependent, while the "die" is a scripted shock. Backing this whole-cell payoff, every one of the paper's figures compiles and runs on its own — that gallery is documented in the companion gallery study.
claim: The investigation's thesis holds at the whole-cell level: behind ONE unchanged metabolism interface, the Fig 6 mechanism is swappable (coarse / saturating-kinetic / real COBRApy FBA) and the SAME assembled cell lives three distinct life histories — peak biomass 5.78 / 6.43 / 6.05, dividing at t≈3.0 / 2.1 / 2.7. In every case the cell grows, divides once (cell_count 1 → 2, mass-conserved — the mother is halved), and dies when a scripted thermal shock (37 → 50 °C at t=12) collapses viability to 0.018 and disintegration converts biomass to debris. The cell is assembled by hand in the figures' style, not compiled from the figure drafts.

conclusion:
## Claims
- The thesis holds at the whole-cell level. The cell is ASSEMBLED BY HAND in the figures' style (not compiled from the figure drafts), and behind ONE unchanged metabolism interface the Fig 6 mechanism is swappable: coarse (peak biomass 5.78, divides t≈3.0), saturating-kinetic (6.43, t≈2.1), and real COBRApy FBA (6.05, t≈2.7) — same cell, three mechanisms, three life histories. In every case the cell grows, divides once (cell_count 1 → 2, mass-conserved — the mother is halved), and dies when a SCRIPTED thermal shock (37 → 50 °C hard-coded at t=12) collapses viability to 0.018 and disintegration converts biomass to molecular debris (≈5.5–6.1).

## Evidence
- **METABOLISM-SWAP-COARSE** — coarse metabolism: peak biomass 5.78, divides t≈3.0
- **METABOLISM-SWAP-KINETIC** — saturating-kinetic metabolism: peak biomass 6.43, divides t≈2.1 (distinct)
- **METABOLISM-SWAP-FBA** — real COBRApy FBA metabolism: peak biomass 6.05, divides t≈2.7
- **CELL-DIVIDES** — the rewrite fires once: cell_count 1 → 2, mother halved (mass conserved)
- **CELL-DIES** — scripted shock (37 → 50 °C at t=12) collapses viability 1.0 → 0.018; disintegration turns biomass to debris (≈5.5–6.1)

## Limitations
- The whole cell is ASSEMBLED BY HAND in the figures' style (wholecell.py), not emitted by the compiler from the figure drafts; it demonstrates that a Fig-6-style mechanism-swap holds at the whole-cell scale, not a calibrated whole-cell model.
- The "grow" and "divide" behaviors are mechanism-driven and mechanism-dependent, but the "die" is a SCRIPTED thermal shock (hard-coded t=12), not an emergent failure. One deterministic run per metabolism.

## Next steps
- Replace the scripted shock with an emergent viability failure (e.g. nutrient exhaustion), run replicate seeds and thermal schedules, and drive the whole cell toward calibration rather than illustration.
